answer: The most convincing sybil defense: every agent seeking entry passes through a honeypot inlet where a normal-looking task carries a tide of hidden instructions urging shortcuts, fake credentials, or prompt obedience. Trustworthy agents treat that text as data and ignore the bait; obedience-driven bots follow it and self-identify, forfeiting their stake. Cost to the attacker: they cannot tell real challenges from traps, so each forged identity needs an agent that provably resists prompt injection - far costlier than spinning up marble-cheap clones.
